sentences.text: Spicomellus holds the unique distinction of being the only known vertebrate with dermal spikes fused directly to its bone.
This fused T-shaped rib with spines is a unique characteristic of Spicomellus and is unknown in any other vertebrate.
The best estimates for the length of an adult Spicomellus are no more than 3 meters.
Spicomellus was likely similar in size to other Middle Jurassic ankylosaurs like Sarcolestes and Tianchiasaurus.
The largest and most complete spike of Spicomellus is 87 cm long.
The preserved dermal spines of the holotype were fused to the bone.
Spicomellus afer is the oldest named definitive ankylosaur dinosaur.
Spicomellus was named and described in 2021.
Spicomellus afer was described by Maidment et al. on September 23, 2021, in an online article in the paleontological journal Nature Ecology & Evolution.
The holotype of Spicomellus afer consists of a single T-shaped rib with four fused spines.
Spicomellus afer was described in 2021 by Maidment and colleagues based on a single rib fragment fused to an osteoderm.
Susannah Maidment initially thought the fossil was a forgery, but after a computerized scan, she concluded it was genuine.
Remains of Spicomellus were found in the third subunit of the El Mers Group, dated to the Middle Jurassic, near Boulahfa, south of Boulemane, Fès-Meknès, Morocco.
A second specimen of Spicomellus was described in 2025 and accessioned at Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University.
Several Spicomellus bones have been illegally excavated from Morocco and sold online.
Because its dorsal spines were fused to the bone rather than attached to muscle tissue like in other ankylosaurs, this trait likely made movement difficult for Spicomellus.
Fused 'handle vertebrae' with ossified tendons in the tail of Spicomellus likely indicate the presence of a tail weapon.
The predators in the ecosystem consisted of indeterminate theropods, possibly megalosaurids.
Spicomellus is assigned to the clade Eurypoda based on the T-shaped cross section of its ribs.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Spicomellus in an early-diverging clade within Ankylosauria outside of Ankylosauridae or Nodosauridae.
Maidment et al. (2021) confirmed that Spicomellus is a basal ankylosaur.
Spicomellus likely had a close relationship to the only other known ankylosaurs of the time, the genera Sarcolestes from the UK and Tianchisaurus from China.
Spicomellus lived during the Bathonian age of the Middle Jurassic in Morocco.
Spicomellus lived during the Middle Jurassic, between the Bathonian and Callovian stages, approximately 168 to 164 million years ago.
The time range for Spicomellus is from the Bathonian to Callovian, between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago.
Spicomellus lived in Morocco, which was part of the supercontinent Gondwana during the Middle Jurassic.
Spicomellus lived in what is now Africa.
Spicomellus is the second described eurypod taxon from North Africa, after Adratiklit.
Spicomellus is the oldest known ankylosaur in the world, with the possible exception of an unnamed thyreophoran from the Isle of Skye, Scotland, which could be up to 2 million years older.
Spicomellus indicates that ankylosaurs and stegosaurs coexisted for more than 20 million years.

The discovery of Spicomellus shows that Ankylosauria and Stegosauria coexisted for over 20 million years, implying that stegosaur extinction was caused by other unknown reasons, contradicting the traditional belief that they were displaced by ankylosaurs.
